events.title: Godfrey of Bouillon Chosen to Lead Jerusalem
events.description: Days after the First Crusade captured Jerusalem, the knight Godfrey of Bouillon was elected the first Protector (Defender) of the Holy Sepulchre. He took this title rather than that of king.
events.significance: It marked the founding of the Crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem, which shaped the politics of the Middle East for nearly two centuries.

events.title: Battle of Falkirk
events.description: Edward I of England and his longbowmen defeated William Wallace's Scottish spear formations outside Falkirk.
events.significance: The defeat ended Wallace's role as a leading commander in the Wars of Scottish Independence. It also showed how powerful massed longbowmen could be on the battlefield.

events.title: Gia Long Unifies Vietnam
events.description: Gia Long conquered Hanoi, bringing an end to centuries of feudal conflict. He became ruler of a unified Vietnam.
events.significance: This laid the foundation for the Nguyen dynasty, the last ruling dynasty of Vietnam, and for the modern Vietnamese state.

events.title: Wiley Post Completes the First Solo Flight Around the World
events.description: American aviator Wiley Post landed at Floyd Bennett Field in Brooklyn after a flight of about seven days and nineteen hours. He had flown alone around the globe.
events.significance: The feat showed how far long-distance aviation and navigation had advanced. It made Post one of the most celebrated pilots of his era.

events.title: King David Hotel Bombing
events.description: The Irgun, a Zionist underground organization, bombed the King David Hotel in Jerusalem. The hotel housed the British administrative and military headquarters for Mandatory Palestine, and 91 people were killed.
events.significance: It was one of the deadliest attacks of the period. It deepened the crisis that preceded the end of British rule in Palestine.
